evidence.reading: run_progress_thread pushes every received event into a Vec unconditionally, alongside rendering it, and returns that Vec through ProgressHandle::join. The two callers use the return value differently. The training path consumes it: training.rs :107 binds handle.join() to events and :111 passes &events to setup.build_training_output, so retention there is load-bearing. The simulation path does not: simulation.rs :66 starts the same thread and :108 drops the result with 'let _ = handle.join();'. Every event the simulation phase emits is therefore retained for the whole phase and then thrown away. The emission rate is one event per scenario: crates/cobre-sddp/src/simulation/state.rs :559 (cited as context) calls emit_sim_progress once per completed scenario inside the scenario loop, and emit_sim_progress (simulation/pipeline.rs :972) sends TrainingEvent::SimulationProgress whenever a sender exists — which is whenever the run is not quiet, per the 'if ctx.quiet' gate at simulation.rs :62. evidence.command: git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-python/src/model.rs | grep -n 'fn buses\|fn lines\|fn thermals\|fn hydros\|fn contracts\|fn pumping_stations\|fn non_controllable_sources\|fn from_arc'; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-python/src/model.rs | sed -n '406,413p'

PyBus::deficit_segments at :51 has the same per-access shape, rebuilding a Vec<Bound<PyDict>> each time it is read. positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/run/setup.rs::resolve_thread_count and the one-time rayon global pool in setup_communicator
positives.why: Lens target 2 examined and clean. The thread count is resolved exactly once (git grep for resolve_thread_count at the pin returns one non-test call site, setup.rs:184), the rayon global pool is built once beside it, the effective count is validated against zero and stored as RunContext.n_threads, and every consumer reads ctx.n_threads (training.rs, simulation.rs, the metadata builders, the summary printer). Nothing re-derives the count and no second pool is constructed; the fallback to current_num_threads on a failed build_global warns instead of silently diverging.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-python/src/run.rs::run_in_scoped_pool
positives.why: The bindings deliberately build a fresh scoped pool per call instead of a process-global one, with the reason stated in the doc comment: a global pool can only be configured once per process, so two sequential run invocations with different thread counts would otherwise silently share the first one. Pool construction failure is an explicit error rather than an implicit fallback. Worth protecting - the per-call pool is a correctness property of a long-lived interpreter, not overhead to remove.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/broadcast.rs::broadcast_value length prefix
positives.why: The two collectives per value are deliberate, not redundant: a broadcast length of zero is the rank-0 failure signal that lets every rank return an error in lockstep instead of deadlocking. Merging the four setup broadcasts into one payload to save collectives would remove that signal and, per CD-002 guidance, a second carrier or tuple redesign on this function is out of bounds - so it is explicitly not recommended here.
positives.sanctionedBy: CD-002 (live, sharpen-only) and the function doc comment

positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/run/simulation.rs drain thread in run_simulation_phase
positives.why: Per-scenario Parquet writing runs on a drain thread fed by a bounded channel, so writing overlaps solving instead of collecting rows for a rank-0 gather - the in-file comment records that the gather alternative overflows i32 on large cases. The same shape exists on the Python path. This is the overlap pattern the training-output write chain lacks, and it is the reason that claim has a concrete target shape.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/run/simulation.rs::merge_simulation_metadata and the pre-collective outcome reconcile
positives.why: Wall clock is reduced with Max, not Sum, because it is the slowest rank's time, and the per-rank outcome is reconciled before the first post-simulate collective so a failure on a strict subset of ranks cannot strand healthy ranks in the allreduce. Both are correct and load-bearing; neither is a cost to remove.

positives.subject: cobre-io writers reached from outputs.rs (write_paths, write_scenario_summary, write_solver_stats)
positives.why: The per-write create_dir_all named as a lens target is not a smell: it is one idempotent metadata call per output file, and it is not duplicated inside the atomic write - ensure_parent_dir is called by write_batch_atomic only, not by write_parquet_atomic, so the writers that create the directory themselves do it once. Removing it would make each writer depend on a caller-created tree for no measurable gain.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/run/setup.rs::reconstruct_stochastic_context_non_root
positives.why: Ownership of the non-root stochastic rebuild is settled and correct: the rebuild routes through cobre-sddp build_stochastic_context_for_study, the same derivation the rank-0 prepare path uses, so it cannot drift across the crate boundary - which is what makes the MPI reproducibility requirement in the comment hold. Only the filesystem cost of the case-directory argument is raised, and as a cost claim, not as a re-raise of the ownership question.
positives.sanctionedBy: CD-001, retired at the cobre-sddp station gate (commits b051c410 / 4075c4e8)

positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/run/training.rs::aggregate_solver_stats
positives.why: The training-side stats fold is a single pass over the convergence log that filters foreign ranks in the same pass and accumulates in place with no per-entry clone - the shape the simulation-side aggregation should adopt.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/progress.rs::create_bar and crates/cobre-cli/src/progress.rs::BarRenderer
positives.why: Answers the lens question directly: the bar is not redrawn per event. create_bar builds its draw target with ProgressDrawTarget::term_like_with_hz(Box::new(MpiTerm{inner, width}), 8), so indicatif rate-limits every redraw regardless of event arrival rate. Both bars are created at most once, through training_bar.get_or_insert_with and simulation_bar.get_or_insert_with, and BarRenderer::handle does one set_position plus one set_message per IterationSummary or SimulationProgress. The two Term::stderr().write_line calls sit in the TrainingFinished and SimulationFinished arms, once per run each. Ten of the fifteen TrainingEvent variants land in a single empty match arm, so the per-iteration telemetry events cost nothing to render. Correct and worth protecting.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/progress.rs::LineRenderer
positives.why: One Term::write_line per rendered event with no throttle, and that is the contract rather than a smell. RenderMode::auto selects RenderMode::Log when Term::stderr().is_term() is false, and the Log variant's own doc says ANSI cursor escapes cannot be interpreted live in pipes, files or mpirun aggregators and would appear as duplicated output otherwise. Throttling or coalescing those lines would change the rendered stderr text, which is exactly what the byte-neutrality bar forbids a fix from doing. The cost is bounded at one line per training iteration and one per simulation scenario, with fmt_sci, fmt_time_cell and fmt_avg_lp_time allocating only within that line.
positives.sanctionedBy: rule 8 byte-neutrality bar — for the shell the rendered stderr text is the contract the CLI tests pin

positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/validate.rs::execute running prepare_stochastic
positives.why: The expensive step is deliberate and must stay. The call site carries its own justification — the most expensive step (PAR estimation, opening trees); validate runs it anyway so an exit-0 guarantees full parity with run — and the module doc states the same exit-0 contract. Removing or short-circuiting PAR estimation would weaken that guarantee, so the cost is the feature. This is recorded as a positive exactly as the lens block requires; the separate candidate above concerns a duplicate boundary resolve, which is avoidable without touching this contract.
positives.sanctionedBy: crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/validate.rs module doc — the exit-0 validation contract

positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/validate.rs case-bundle and config parsing
positives.why: Examined for a repeated parse and it is not there. validate_case_with_artifacts returns the pre-parsed CaseArtifacts that the hydro-models phase reuses (the call site says so: avoiding a second disk read, and the later call passes &artifacts to reuse the already-parsed bundle). cobre_io::CaseArtifacts, at crates/cobre-io/src/lib.rs (cited as context), holds eight fields and no Config, and 'git grep -n parse_config( 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-io/src | grep -v tests' shows the only non-doc declaration is parse_config itself, so the case loader never parses config.json. The single cobre_io::parse_config call in execute is the only parse of that file.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/summary.rs
positives.why: Non-test lines are one-shot formatting. Every print_ and format_ function runs once per phase, and the only loops outside the inline test module are the host walk in print_execution_topology and the segment walk in format_rank_list, both bounded by the run's host and rank counts and executed once. The per-hydro line loop the lens asked about does not exist: HydroModelSummary is an aggregate of counts, not a per-entity collection, so there is nothing to iterate. Nothing here sits on a per-iteration or per-scenario path.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/error.rs::format_error and the From impls
positives.why: The formatting path runs once, at the end of the process. format_error writes one to three lines immediately before std::process::exit, and each From impl allocates one String for one fatal error. No loop, no repetition, no per-iteration call site.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/templates.rs and crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/init.rs::execute_scaffold
positives.why: The byte copies the lens asked about are compile-time, not runtime. The module doc states that all file bytes are embedded via include_bytes! so the registry is allocation-free; the template list is a static slice and find_template is a linear scan over ALL_TEMPLATES's single entry. execute_scaffold does one create_dir_all on the parent plus one fs::write per embedded file, and pin_schema_urls allocates one String per JSON file through str::replace. positives.subject: crates/cobre-cli/src/main.rs, crates/cobre-cli/src/banner.rs, crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/schema.rs, crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/version.rs, crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/mod.rs

positives.subject: crates/cobre-python/src/study.rs::Study — the four heavy entry points and the callback drain

This is the pattern the results.rs and io.rs candidates above ask the rest of the crate to match, and it is worth protecting as the reference shape.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-python/src/convert.rs::pydict_to_json_map and ::py_to_json_value

The map is pre-sized with Map::with_capacity(dict.len()), the conversion is a single pass with no intermediate string round-trip, and the module doc states the ordering contract this lens cares about: the override map is converted under the GIL before the solver lifecycle releases it with py.detach. positives.subject: crates/cobre-python/src/io.rs::validate — phase 9 prepare_stochastic
positives.why: Running the most expensive preparation step during validation is a deliberate parity contract with cobre validate, so that a clean validate means the run will not fail in that phase. The candidate raised above is about the GIL being held during that phase, which is orthogonal and leaves the phase and its position in the pipeline untouched.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-python/src/results.rs::load_convergence_arrow, ::load_stochastic, ::load_simulation_arrow

positives.subject: crates/cobre-python/src/results.rs::get_column_by_name as used by load_convergence
positives.why: The correct Arrow access shape in this crate: the 14 typed column views are resolved once per record batch and then indexed per row, so the dynamic downcast is paid per column rather than per cell. It is the in-file model the read_parquet_partition_into candidate points at, and it should stay as it is.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-python/src/policy.rs — the detached checkpoint write with borrowed record views

Only the unconditional coefficient clone that precedes the detach is raised above; the surrounding structure is correct and is what makes that fix small.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-python/src/errors.rs::LeafClass

Each dual-base exception type is built once per interpreter through PyOnceLock::get_or_try_init and cached for the interpreter lifetime, so raising costs a cached type lookup plus one message format rather than a type construction. Error-path string formatting is off any hot path by definition.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-python/src/schema.rs::export and crates/cobre-python/src/version.rs::version_info
positives.why: Examined and clean for this lens. Both are one-shot calls with no per-element conversion, no clone-per-access and no repeated pass: export generates the schema set once and writes each file once, and version_info sets six dict entries from constants and two solver accessors.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-python/src/lib.rs — the module registration surface
positives.why: Examined and clean for this lens. Registration builds the sub-modules and binds the functions and classes once at import time; there is no per-call work and no lazily rebuilt state on any data path.

_needsHuman.question: Rooted gather at L0: the two simulation gathers need a gatherv the cobre-comm Communicator trait does not expose (it has allgatherv, allreduce, broadcast, barrier, rank, size). Adding it grows the L0 surface for two present consumers, both in this file. Is that acceptable, or should the CLI keep allgatherv and accept that every non-root rank allocates and rebuilds a payload it discards?

Is the shared-filesystem re-read on non-root ranks a ratified deployment assumption? The setup.rs module doc states the behaviour with no rationale and no docs/design entry covers it, so replacing the per-rank hydro-model refit (and the per-rank policy-checkpoint read in simulation-only mode) with a rank-0 read plus a broadcast is a trade between collective payload size and filesystem load that only the owner can settle.

Deferring the rank-0 training-artefact write so it overlaps rank 0 entering the simulation phase changes the stderr progress ordering (Writing training outputs appears interleaved with simulation progress) and makes the checkpoint write compete for I/O bandwidth with the simulation drain writes. Is the stderr ordering free to change, given the byte-neutrality bar covers the output tree and the validate --json stdout contract only?

Sequencing for the duplicate boundary resolve in validate.rs: patch it now as a cli-local parameter thread, or hold it and let CD-029's approved fold of the boundary check into cobre-sddp PrepPhase subsume it? The fold would make the requirements a phase input resolved once, so taking both in order means touching the same call chain twice. Rule 5 already holds the fold destination itself as a needs-human for the gate, so the cost argument should be decided with it rather than ahead of it.

Is the dict-shaped cobre.results.load_simulation still a supported bulk reader, or is load_simulation_arrow now the intended path for large result trees? The answer decides whether the per-cell Arrow dispatch in read_parquet_partition_into is worth fixing or whether the dict reader should instead be documented as a small-result convenience, and it is a user-facing API posture question the station cannot settle.

May load_results bind one converted object to both the manifest and metadata keys of the training dict, making them the same Python object and aliasing on mutation, or must they stay two equal-but-distinct dicts? Collapsing the double conversion is only byte-neutral in values, not in object identity, so the owner decides whether identity is part of the published contract.
